message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on cables for the Zulu aviation headset. The cables are insulated conductors fitted with a connector at one end only, so they are not "fitted with connectors" at both ends in the sense of a finished cable assembly. Heading 8544 covers insulated wire, cable and other insulated electric conductors, whether or not fitted with connectors.

Subheading 8544.42 covers conductors for a voltage not exceeding 1,000 V that are fitted with connectors. Within it, 8544.42.90 is "Other", and 8544.42.20 covers conductors of a kind used for telecommunications. Because these carry audio signals and power at low voltage, they fall under 8544.42.

Within 8544.42.90, the statistical suffix is 8544.42.9090. Subheading 8544.42.20 is for telecommunications, and a headset cable is not clearly that. I am going with 8544.42.9090.

{"hts_code": "8544.42.9090", "reason": "Insulated electric conductors of not more than 1,000 V fitted with a connector at one end, used for audio, power and noise-cancellation signals in a headset, fall under heading 8544, subheading 8544.42, in the 'Other' provision."}
